rule: An entry is relevant to a brief if someone doing that work would want to see it, in any of these roles — `use` (could use it directly), `similar` (does something close; could copy the approach), `same-problem` (hit or solved the same problem), `guide` (a strategy, philosophy, or lesson that applies). A passing mention or a shared word alone is not enough.

roles.similar: does something close; could copy the approach
roles.same-problem: hit or solved the same problem
roles.guide: a strategy, philosophy, or lesson that applies

briefs.question: I have a laptop with a 16 GB GPU and 64 GB of RAM, and I want to run Qwen 3.8 or other open-weight models locally for agentic coding, where a long context window matters more than speed. Later I may use a 24 GB or 48 GB card. What do we have for picking and setting up models at each of those sizes?

I'm building a knowledge and memory system for coding agents: typed markdown records linked in a deterministic graph, searched lexically, with semantic embeddings being added. What do we have on RAG and on this kind of hybrid search, so I can see how my approach compares?
I want to vibe code a cozy 3D survival game, generating the art and sound and building procedural levels. I've never made a game. What services, tools, approaches, and ideas do we have?

I build a tool that dispatches coding agents to run tasks in the background. I want a live view of the agents while they work, like zoetrope (I think that's the name): who is running, what they are doing, and when one hangs. A terminal view or a web page both work. What do we have?

I'm benchmarking ways to turn scientific PDFs (clinical trials, papers with complex figures, table-heavy genomics papers) into markdown: CPU parsers, small vision models on a 16 GB GPU, and a hosted API, against a frontier-LLM agent as the baseline. What do we have on models, approaches, scoring, and setup that I could learn from or add?

I want to benchmark how a wiki of linked markdown records, used as the memory for my coding projects, holds up as it grows from tens to a thousand records: how long indexing, search, and linting take, and whether search still finds the right records. What do we have?

I save videos, docs, and courses as markdown notes and track my projects in a wiki. I think we have something called "learn anything", plus other skills and tools, for organizing files, ideas, and work into a simply explained system. What are they?
